title: ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral
gist: ClickFix, in which a compromised site shows a fake Cloudflare-style CAPTCHA and instructs the visitor to paste a single command into Windows Run, PowerShell or the macOS terminal, has gone mainstream because it eliminates the expensive delivery infrastructure malware operators previously needed. BlueVoyant documented a late-May 2026 pivot that dropped code-signing entirely, Netskope counted 5,400 sites beaconing to one campaign, macOS variants bypass Gatekeeper, and Russia's Sandworm is hosting control infrastructure in blockchain smart contracts.

insights.claim: Before ClickFix, operators of the malware tracked as Lorem Ipsum needed resource-intensive infrastructure including SEO-manipulated and malvertised download portals, Microsoft-trusted signing certificates, and continuously rotated domains delivering Microsoft Installer packages.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The baseline cost structure of malware delivery is what ClickFix destroys; anything that lowers attacker capex expands the attacker population.
insights.locator: For the people behind the attacks

insights.claim: BlueVoyant says the pivot to ClickFix in late May 2026 eliminated the code-signing requirement entirely, substituting a validly signed installer's legitimacy with a different form of legitimacy: a user voluntarily executing the malicious command in their own terminal.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Code-signing and certificate-reputation defenses, a core pillar of endpoint security products, are simply routed around by this technique.
insights.quote: The pivot to ClickFix in late May 2026 eliminates the code-signing requirement entirely, substituting the legitimacy of a validly signed installer with a different form of legitimacy
insights.locator: For the people behind the attacks

insights.claim: The ClickFix model broadens the victim pool from users specifically searching for a targeted product such as Microsoft Teams to anyone browsing a compromised website.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Targeting shifts from intent-based to opportunistic, which raises expected infection volume and therefore the demand for browser-level and paste-level controls.
insights.quote: ClickFix model broadens the victim pool from users searching specifically for Microsoft Teams to anyone browsing a compromised website
insights.locator: For the people behind the attacks

insights.claim: The entire attack requires only a compromised website, a fake CAPTCHA overlay and a single terminal command, and its simplicity and effectiveness have led just about every malware pusher to adopt it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Near-universal adoption across threat actors means detection signatures tied to any single payload family will miss the bulk of incidents.
insights.locator: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic

insights.claim: Casual users have been desensitized to ridiculous and burdensome instructions because normal computing already requires impossible-to-close interstitials, endless picture CAPTCHAs and constantly changing interfaces that bury features.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Legitimate friction in web UX is the substrate the attack exploits, implying that reducing dark patterns and CAPTCHA burden is itself a security control.
insights.locator: How many of us make things worse

insights.claim: The prompts appear on websites people have used for years and the directions seem no more suspicious than things they have been required to do for a decade, giving non-experts no reason to hesitate.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Domain reputation and site familiarity are no longer usable trust signals for end users, weakening awareness-training approaches built on 'check the URL.'
insights.quote: The instructions come from websites people have used for years.

insights.claim: The author argues victim-blaming and shaming of users who fall for ClickFix only makes the problem worse, and that security-literate people should build awareness among less experienced neighbors, family and friends.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Frames the residual defense as social rather than technical, a tacit admission that product-level controls are currently insufficient.
insights.quote: It’s not going away, and victim-blaming or shaming only makes the problem worse.

insights.claim: Independent researcher Kevin Beaumont observed that Reddit is filling with post after post of people getting infected via ClickFix and that legitimate websites everywhere are being hacked to serve fake CAPTCHA prompts.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Consumer-visible infection volume is the leading indicator that this has moved from targeted campaigns to mass-market compromise.
insights.quote: Reddit is becoming post after post after post of people getting their computer infected via ClickFix
insights.locator: How many of us make things worse

insights.claim: Mac security firm Jamf and an independent researcher have documented macOS variations of ClickFix that bypass Gatekeeper protections, removing the assumption that Apple's platform gatekeeping blunts the technique.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Mac-fleet risk is converging with Windows, which supports demand for endpoint security spend in Mac-heavy organizations that previously underinvested.
insights.locator: The situation for macOS users isn’t any better

insights.claim: Attackers are abusing public services for delivery, including publicly published Google Sheets documents according to Cisco Talos, while Russia's state-sponsored Sandworm and others host control infrastructure in blockchain-based smart contracts.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Smart-contract command-and-control is effectively untakedownable, which shifts defense from infrastructure disruption to endpoint execution control.
insights.locator: ClickFix attackers keep finding new ways

insights.claim: Netskope found a ClickFix campaign with 5,400 sites beaconing to it, an indication of the reach and scope of a single operation.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A concrete scale metric for one campaign, useful for calibrating how widely compromised-site inventories now serve this lure.
insights.locator: Security firm Netskope recently found another campaign

insights.claim: Kremlin-backed hacking groups have adopted ClickFix alongside commodity criminals, collapsing the usual distinction between state-sponsored tradecraft and mass-market malware delivery.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: When state actors use the same low-cost vector as criminals, attribution and prioritization get harder for defenders and insurers alike.
insights.quote: Even Kremlin-backed hacking groups are joining in.
insights.locator: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic

insights.claim: Existing countermeasures act at the paste step: BlockBlock can block ClickFix attacks on Macs as soon as a user presses Command+V, and uBlock has been updated to do something similar, but attackers keep finding documented ways around new OS defenses.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Clipboard-level interception is the emerging control point; watch for OS vendors and endpoint suites to build this natively.
insights.locator: There are a fair number of plugins
